MSFT.rationale: Microsoft presents a strong fundamental case with excellent health trajectory, tempered by a valuation that is no longer clearly cheap after the recent recovery. Pillar 1 (Fundamentals): Q3 FY2026 showed 18.3% YoY revenue growth to $82.9B, 23.1% YoY net income growth, and Azure accelerating to 40% growth. Operating margin expanded 60bps to 46.3%. The balance sheet is fortress-like with $78.3B cash vs $40.3B debt. AI business run rate hit $37B (up 123% YoY). M365 Copilot crossed 20M paid seats with 250% YoY growth. The business model is transitioning to license-plus-consumption, which should better monetize AI compute. However, QoQ EPS declined 17.2% (from $5.16 to $4.27), and gross margin compressed to 67.6% from 68.7% due to AI infrastructure costs. The $190B 2026 capex plan (vs $154.6B consensus) signals margin pressure ahead, with Q4 capex guided to exceed $40B. Pillar 2 (Valuation): At PE 29.8x and EV/EBIT 22.6x, MSFT trades near the low end of its 12-month range (PE 25.4-42.8, EV/EBIT 19.2-34.1). The stock is down ~24% from its 52-week high of $555.45 to $419.09. This is meaningfully cheaper than the 35-40x PE range that prevailed through most of 2025, but not at distressed levels. The valuation is fair-to-slightly-cheap relative to its own history, offering moderate upside if execution continues. Pillar 3 (Near-term catalyst): The OpenAI partnership restructuring (April 27) caps revenue share at $38B, accelerates $6B cash flow to 2026, and extends IP licensing through 2032 — improving long-term margin profile. Q4 FY2026 earnings (July 29) will be a key catalyst as new data center capacity comes online and Azure growth is expected to accelerate beyond 40%. The UK CMA antitrust probe (opened May 14, concluding Feb 2027) introduces regulatory overhang but is not imminent. Overall: excellent franchise with accelerating AI monetization, but massive capex cycle and margin compression cap the upside. The stock is attractively positioned in its valuation range but not a screaming bargain.

M365 Copilot crossed 20M paid seats (250% YoY growth) with only 4.4% of 450M M365 base converted — massive runway
$190B 2026 capex plan exceeded consensus by $35B, with $25B attributed to component inflation; gross margin compressed to 67.6%
PE of 29.8x is near the low end of 12-month range (25.4-42.8), down from 35-40x through most of 2025
OpenAI restructuring caps revenue share at $38B, extends IP licensing through 2032, and accelerates $6B cash flow
Balance sheet strength: $78.3B cash vs $40.3B debt, net cash of $38B
UK CMA antitrust probe opened May 14 into Microsoft's business software bundling — regulatory overhang
Q4 FY2026 earnings (July 29) as near-term catalyst with new capacity coming online and Azure expected to accelerate beyond 40%

sources_cited.excerpt: Revenue from AI business surged 123% year-on-year, with an annual run rate of US$37 billion. M365 Copilot surged 250% year-on-year to surpass 20 million paid seats. Operating margin improved from 45.7% to 46.3%

2026 calendar capex plan of approximately $190 billion, which exceeded analyst consensus of $154.6 billion by roughly $35 billion, and the explicit attribution of $25 billion of that figure to component price inflation
Azure grew 40% in Q3 FY2026 and holds roughly 21–24% of the global cloud infrastructure market. Only 20 million of Microsoft's 450 million M365 commercial subscribers pay for Copilot — about 4.4%
Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation has completed its exit from Microsoft by selling its final 7.7 million shares worth $3.2 billion in Q1 2026
Bill Ackman's Pershing Square Capital Management has added Microsoft as a fourth Magnificent Seven stock, built the position in February when the stock traded at 21x forward earnings
